items.title: Bond role was ‘Josh O’Connor’s to lose’ but actor pulled out of the running, report suggests
items.summary: The Crown star was reportedly an early favourite of director Denis Villeneuve, but ‘had reservations about the baggage associated with the role from the start’ Josh O’Connor, one of the actors on the final shortlist for the role of James Bond which was ultimately won by Robert Pattinson, was an early favourite of director Denis Villeneuve but pulled out of the contest before a decision was made, it has been reported. Writing in Puck’s What I’m Hearing newsletter , Matthew Belloni (who correctly forecast that Pattinson would win the role ) said that O’Connor “had reservations about the baggage associated with the role from the start” and pulled out shortly after his test. items.summary: With its policy priorities more mainstream than ever, the left is directing its momentum toward 2028 A week after the US midterm elections swept an unprecedented number of leftists into office across the country, about 600 people joined a Zoom call. The goal: to convince Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez to run for president. On the call, organizers from Ready for AOC, a new group of progressive and labor organizers, wasted little time celebrating the Democrats’ electoral sweep. “People all over the country are ready for a much different and much better future,” said Genevieve Rand, an organizer with the group. “We are more ready than we have ever been.” Continue reading...

items.summary: Since the spacecraft’s 1977 launch, our wonderful and terrible species has done great damage to our planet. Voyager has offered us a clear view of ourselves Imagine traveling nonstop for 49 years, alone in the dark with no destination in sight, powered by curiosity and engineering. Further imagine making that journey not at bullet train or jet plane speed, but much faster: at 37,800 miles per hour, free from friction in a vast sea of cold, soundless space, bombarded by radiation and cosmic rays yet still able to communicate with folks back home. items.title: Grand Theft Auto VI review – gaming’s most depraved world is now also its greatest love story
items.summary: With realism that defies belief, this vast game easily accommodates its trademark foulmouthed, OTT chaos – as well as new empathy for the fugitive couple at its centre Tell us: are you playing Grand Theft Auto VI? In GTA VI, Rockstar has created the most extraordinarily, indulgently detailed virtual world that we have yet seen. Reviewing it feels a bit like trying to review, say, Paris: it contains so many potential experiences that it’s hard to know where to start.
